message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | # | What Happens | How It Works | |---|--------------|--------------| | 1 | **Setup** | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. | | 2 | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (or counterclockwise if a “Reverse” card is played). | | 3 | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play **one** card that matches the **color** or **number/symbol** of the top discard. If you can’t, you must draw one card. | | 4 | **Special Cards** | • **Skip** – Next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses play direction.
• **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and loses a turn.
• **Wild** – You choose the next color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – You choose the next color; next player draws four cards and loses a turn (must be played only if you have no matching color). | | 5 | **Winning a Turn** | If you play your last card, shout “UNO!” when you have one card left. If you’re the first to get rid of all your cards, you win the round. | | 6 | **Scoring** | • After a round ends, players score points from the cards left in opponents’ hands:
 – Number cards: face value.
 – Draw Two, Reverse, Skip: 20 points.
 – Wild, Wild Draw Four: 50 points.
• First player to reach 500 points (or another agreed total) wins the game. | **Key Tips** - Keep track of the current color; if you play a Wild, remember to announce the new color. - If you’re forced to draw a card and it’s playable, you may play it immediately. - “Wild Draw Four” can be challenged: if the challenged player can play a card of the announced color, they win the challenge and you must draw four cards instead. That’s the core of Uno! Feel free to add house rules (e.g., “Draw Two” stacks, “Skip” stacks) to spice things up. Enjoy the game!
